h1: True cost of real estate commission Calculator
summary: Give the True cost of real estate commission calculator the property price, the down payment, the seller's commission and the term and it returns buyer's commission. It suits a budget, a loan conversation, a payslip check or a what-if before you talk to a lender. The formula is printed further down, so you can check the answer by hand if you want to.

sections.title: How does the True cost of real estate commission calculator work?
sections.html:
The True cost of real estate commission calculator takes the values in the form, applies the relationship described below and reports buyer's commission in the results panel.

Working from the top of the form: you type in the property price, the down payment, the seller's commission and the term.

The arithmetic runs locally each time an input changes. The page knows which values you have given it and which it still has to derive, so the results panel is never stale.

Because the equation can be rearranged for each of its variables, the page also runs backwards. Leave the box you want to know empty, fill in the rest, and it solves for the missing one instead. That is useful when you know the answer you need rather than the inputs you have.

sections.title: The formula behind the True cost of real estate commission calculator
sections.html:
The page rests on a handful of relationships. Each one can be rearranged for any of its variables, which is what makes the calculator work in both directions:

Buyer's commission=(down payment − property price + loan amount) ÷ property price
Monthly payment=(interest rate × loan amount × (interest rate + 1 ^ term) ÷ ((interest rate + 1 ^ term) − 1))
...of which the commission is=(interest rate × (interest rate + 1 ^ term) × the smaller of (-down payment + property price, (property price × (buyer's commission + seller's commission))) ÷ ((interest rate + 1 ^ term) − 1))
Total payments=(term × (interest rate × loan amount × (interest rate + 1 ^ term) ÷ ((interest rate + 1 ^ term) − 1)))
Real commission cost=(term × (interest rate × (interest rate + 1 ^ term) × the smaller of (-down payment + property price, (property price × (buyer's commission + seller's commission))) ÷ ((interest rate + 1 ^ term) − 1)) + (property price × (buyer's commission + seller's commission)) − the smaller of (-down payment + property price, (property price × (buyer's commission + seller's commission))))
Commission amount=(property price × (buyer's commission + seller's commission))

Read it as an ordinary equation. Where a word appears instead of a letter, it is the label of one of the boxes in the form; where a function appears, it is the usual mathematical meaning of that function.

If a number looks wrong, check three things in this order: that the units match what you had in mind, that no drop-down is still on its default, and that the value you entered is on the same scale as the rest — a rate typed as 5 rather than 0.05 is the classic mistake. Those three account for almost every answer that is out by a factor.

sections.title: How are units and precision handled?
sections.html:
Every quantity with units carries a chip beside its box. Switching the chip does not change what you know, only how it is written: values are converted to a common internal base, the arithmetic happens there, and the answer is converted back for display. Mixing metres with feet in one calculation is therefore safe.

Results are rounded for display but computed at full precision, so chaining one result into the next does not accumulate error. Very large and very small numbers switch to scientific notation rather than printing a run of zeros.

sections.title: When should you use it?
sections.html:
The True cost of real estate commission calculator earns its place in the middle of a task, not instead of one. It is most useful when:

  • Building a monthly budget and testing how one number shifts the rest
  • Comparing two offers that quote their costs in different ways
  • Preparing questions for a lender, an accountant or an adviser
  • Any time the same 4 figures keep coming back — the property price, the down payment and the seller's commission — and you would rather not repeat the arithmetic by hand each time.

sections.title: How do you get a reliable answer?
sections.html:
• Change one input at a time when you are exploring. Two simultaneous changes make it impossible to tell which one moved the result.
  • If a result surprises you, look at the order of magnitude before the digits: a plausible number in the wrong unit looks more convincing than an implausible one, and is easier to miss.
  • Leave the field you want solved for empty rather than guessing at it. Filling every box tells the calculator you already know the answer.
  • Compare two scenarios by changing the input that actually differs between them, and keep the rest fixed, so the difference you see is the difference you meant to test.

sections.title: What else is worth knowing?
sections.html:
• Filling in more than one box is fine. The most recently edited field is the one treated as known, so you can switch direction without reloading.
  • Fields that are still blank are exactly the ones the calculator has not yet been given, so the results panel is a reliable map of what is missing.

faq.q: What does the True cost of real estate commission calculator work out?
faq.a: It returns buyer's commission, derived from the property price, the down payment and the seller's commission. Every field in the form feeds the same relationship: press Calculate once and changing any of them updates the result immediately, with no page reload.

faq.q: What do I need to enter to use the True cost of real estate commission calculator?
faq.a: The form asks for the property price, the down payment, the seller's commission and the term, which is 6 fields in total. Each one is labelled with what it means and, where relevant, the unit it expects. Anything you leave blank is treated as the value to solve for.

faq.q: Can I enter property price in a different unit?
faq.a: Yes. Property price opens in US Dollar and the chip beside it offers 113 units. The number you typed keeps its magnitude and only its label changes; the calculation itself happens in a common base unit, so mixing systems in one form is safe.
Yes. Each variable in the relationship can be the one being solved for: fill in the answer you are aiming at, leave the field you want empty, and the calculator inverts the equation for you.

faq.q: Is the True cost of real estate commission calculator free to use?
faq.a: Yes — no account, no sign-up and no limit on how many times you run it. The arithmetic happens in your browser, so the values you type are not sent anywhere.

faq.q: Do I have to fill in every box?
faq.a: Fill in the ones you know. The result boxes are computed from them, so you never enter a value the formula can derive — press Calculate and every result updates together.
